family_title_en: Complete the word with the ending that you hear

stages.ix_title: Complete the word with the ending that you hear

prompt.en: Which word has the right ending?

what_to_do.en: Tap the whole word that fits.

stages.choice_rule: Four different real whole words. Exactly one fits the hyphen in the stem. Prefer other endings of the same base. The correct word must be on the roots list or in allowed_extra_words. Never a bare suffix, a single letter, a non-word, a brand, or a sound symbol.

gold_items.stem: He can ride his bike - to school.
This dog is - than that cat.
My dog is the - dog of all.

roots: Write one Grade 2 sentence about home, school, food, pets, play, family, or weather, with a hyphen where the word is missing.
Stem words must come from the roots word list, allowed extra words, or the NAME token. Do not use a real personal name or a brand.
Give four different real whole words. Exactly one ending fits the hyphen. Prefer four forms of the same base.
The correct choice must be a real word on the roots list or in allowed extra words. Never key a non-word, a bare suffix, or a single letter.
Tier 1 cues are plain: is or are needs ing, yesterday needs ed, and two needs a plural s. Wrong endings should look easy to reject.
Tier 2 uses ly for how, er with than, or y to make a describing word. Wrong choices are other real forms of that word.
Tier 3 is a near miss: est against er, or an irregular past such as swam against swim and swimming. One answer only.
The child reads and taps. Do not use audio files, held sounds, or sound marks between slashes.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of about five to seven words with an obvious cue. is or are needs ing, yesterday needs ed, and two needs the plural s. Wrong choices are the base or a clearly wrong real ending.
tier_rules.2: Grade-level stems. Test ly when the word tells how, er when the sentence has than, and y when the word describes. Wrong choices are other real forms, usually of the same base.
tier_rules.3: Near misses on longer stems. est is right where er is tempting, or an irregular past such as swam is right where swim or swimming is tempting. NAME is allowed. Keep a single right answer.

ing_now.en: After is or are, an action happening now needs the ending ing.
ing_now.ko: is나 are 뒤에는 지금 하는 행동에 끝 ing가 필요합니다.

ed_past.en: A finished action in the past needs the ending ed.
ed_past.ko: 과거에 끝난 행동에는 끝 ed가 필요합니다.

s_plural.en: Use the ending s when the word names more than one thing.
s_plural.ko: 둘 이상의 사물을 나타낼 때는 끝 s를 씁니다.

es_plural.en: After s, x, ch, or sh, more than one thing needs the ending es.
es_plural.ko: s, x, ch, sh 뒤에는 하나가 아니면 끝 es를 붙입니다.

s_verb.en: One doer doing something now can need the ending s on the action word.
s_verb.ko: 하나가 지금 하는 행동에는 동작 말에 끝 s가 붙을 수 있습니다.

ly_how.en: Use the ending ly when the word tells how an action happens.
ly_how.ko: 행동이 어떻게 일어나는지 말할 때는 끝 ly를 씁니다.

er_than.en: Use the ending er to compare two when the sentence has than.
er_than.ko: than으로 둘을 비교할 때는 끝 er를 씁니다.

er_person.en: The ending er can name the person who does a job, like teach and teacher.
er_person.ko: 끝 er는 teach와 teacher처럼 그 일을 하는 사람을 나타낼 수 있습니다.

est_most.en: Of all means the most, so the describing word takes the ending est.
est_most.ko: of all은 가장이라는 뜻이므로 모습 말에 끝 est를 씁니다.

y_describe.en: The ending y makes a describing word, as sun becomes sunny.
y_describe.ko: 끝 y는 sun이 sunny가 되듯 모습을 나타내는 말을 만듭니다.

irregular_past.en: Some past actions keep a special past word that fits the time word.
irregular_past.ko: 어떤 과거 행동은 시간 말에 맞는 특별한 과거 단어를 씁니다.

irregular_plural.en: Some naming words change for more than one, like mouse and mice.
irregular_plural.ko: 어떤 말은 하나가 아니면 mouse와 mice처럼 모양이 바뀝니다.
